clue.text: Beach-tank top unusually seen here gets sign of approval

indicators.note: unusually tells us the letters of the preceding words are arranged in an unusual new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, the rest of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A beachgoer's sleeveless top is so unusual here that it wins applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the twelve letters of BEACH and TANK TOP; 'seen here gets' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Congratulating someone with a friendly tap between the shoulders is the idiom for praise or approval.

clue.text: In black and white, letter Lincoln sent up to lord

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the name is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar name

explanation.surface: A letter from President Lincoln is passed up to a peer, written in black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses ABE to EBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Piebald describes a horse with patches of black and white, so the adjective matches the phrase.

clue.text: Not a characteristic city? Not originally

indicators.note: Not tells us to leave out the letter a from the word for characteristic

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A town with no distinctive feature, and nothing original about it either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a' removes A from TRAIT, leaving TRIT. Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tritely means in a stale, hackneyed way, so done without originality.

clue.text: Almost quaint (but not quite)- a queen's attire

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost

indicators.note: not quite tells us the word for quaint is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: twee means quaintly, sweetly pretty
R is short for rex or regina, so a queen is R

explanation.surface: A queen's outfit is nearly quaint, though not entirely so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not quite' trims TWEE to TWE. 'Twee' is a British word for affectedly quaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is clothing worn in bed, so a kind of attire.

clue.text: Bat that is rescued from small falcons

indicators.note: rescued from means the letters for that is are taken out of the falcons

parts.note: hobbies are small falcons
ie is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A bat is saved from the clutches of little birds of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' is a batsman: Jack Hobbs was a great English cricketer of the early 20th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbs was a celebrated batsman, and in cricket a bat can mean the player batting.

clue.text: Dictionary for those providing drinks

definitions.meaning: ... Dictionary of Phrase and Fable is a classic reference book
people who make beer supply drinks

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the reference book named after Ebenezer Cobham Brewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewer's is a famous dictionary of phrase and fable, and brewers make beer to drink.

clue.text: Little boy hiding in vehicle's body

indicators.note: hiding in says the boy is tucked inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Dave is a short form of the boy's name David

explanation.surface: A small boy is concealed inside a vehicle's bodywork.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a corpse, a dead body.

clue.text: Race? That could be tiptop notion

indicators.note: That could be suggests the letters of tiptop notion could form something new

explanation.surface: A race, the first-rate idea someone had.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is a cross-country steeplechase for amateur riders, a kind of horse race.

clue.text: Opportunity for small number in old office to reflect

indicators.note: to reflect means the built-up letters are mirrored, read from right to left
in places the small number inside the old office

parts.note: GPO is the General Post Office, the former British postal authority
nine is a small number

explanation.surface: A minor official gets a chance to think things over in an old office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small number' is a specific digit spelt out, not N; 'to reflect' reverses the whole result. The GPO (General Post Office) was Britain's old state postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a chance or vacancy, a synonym for an opportunity.

clue.text: Loaf that's half the size

parts.note: a loaf is a quantity of bread

indicators.note: half of the three-letter word the keeps only its front two letters

explanation.surface: A loaf of bread that has shrunk to half its usual dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first two letters of THE, giving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is width, one dimension of an object's size.

clue.text: Let's hold on way to shop

parts.note: to let a property is to hire it out
purchase means grip or hold, as in getting a purchase on a rope

explanation.surface: An instruction to wait on the road to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests waiting, but 'hold' is a grip and the following 'on' only links, as does the 's after 'Let'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire purchase is the British term for buying goods by instalments, one method of shopping.

clue.text: Most accessible organ found in retreat

indicators.note: found in says the organ sits inside the word for retreat

parts.note: a nest is a snug hideaway or retreat
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An organ that is easiest to reach is discovered tucked away in a hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The closest place is the one easiest to get to, so the superlative of near matches most accessible.

clue.text: Inspect diocese from beginning to end

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
over means throughout, from start to finish, as in 'read it over'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to examine a whole diocese thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To look something over closely is a phrasal verb meaning to examine or inspect it.

clue.text: Bear being beset ultimately by troubled water

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word beset

parts.note: an eddy is a swirl of disturbed water

explanation.surface: A bear surrounded by rough water in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes T, the last letter of 'beset'; 'being' and 'by' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy is a toy bear, named after President Theodore Roosevelt.

clue.text: Earwig drove apes mad

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of drove apes go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An insect drives a troop of apes crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earwig' looks like the insect but is the verb: to earwig is to listen in secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is an old informal verb for listening in on a private conversation.

clue.text: Swagger and look inside varying arrangement

indicators.note: inside says the word for look goes within the rearranged letters
arrangement means the letters of varying are rearranged

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Advice to strut about and examine a changeable display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges the seven letters of 'varying' to VAINGRY before 'inside' puts the old exclamation into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainglory is boastful pride, and swagger is a show of arrogant self-importance.

clue.text: From the back, break into observation post, capturing nothing but miscellaneous stuff

indicators.note: From the back means the whole assembled string is read right to left
capturing says the zero is held inside the word for break into

parts.note: to irrupt is to burst or break into a place
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O
OP is the military abbreviation for observation post

explanation.surface: Soldiers storm a lookout post but seize only a jumble of odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' places the zero mid-word, giving IRRUOPT; 'From the back' then reverses IRRUOPTOP, everything at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a mixed collection of assorted things, originally a bowl of dried petals.

clue.text: Excellent work secured by pin

indicators.note: secured by says the work is held inside the pin

parts.note: a thole is a peg on a boat's side used as a rowlock
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A job is fastened with a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: Top-hole is dated British slang for first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hole is old-fashioned British slang meaning first-class or superb.

clue.text: Operational research initially provided to one church in 8

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: if means on condition that, provided
the Roman numeral one is I
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Research findings are passed to a church for a new opening.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to 8 across, OPENING, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or aperture, the same as the solution at 8 across.

clue.text: One produces cracks in rock very centrally

parts.note: Gib is a nickname for Gibraltar, known as the Rock

indicators.note: centrally takes the middle letters of the word very

explanation.surface: Something that splits rock right through the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' are wisecracks or jibes, not fissures; 'centrally' gives ER from 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gibes makes taunting remarks, and cracks are quips or jokes.

clue.text: Fish I cover up in the sea

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an eel is a fish
lag means insulate, cover pipes

explanation.surface: Someone hides a fish under wraps out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: EEL, I and LAG give EELILAG, which 'up' reverses as one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sea of Galilee is the freshwater lake in Israel, where Jesus calmed the storm.

clue.text: Briefly, Indian city's temperature makes for extravagant talk

indicators.note: Briefly means the city's name is cut short

parts.note: Bombay is the former name of Mumbai

explanation.surface: A hot spell in an Indian city leads to grand claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops Y from BOMBAY, keeping the possessive S. Bombay is the old name of Mumbai.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated language with little meaning.

clue.text: Suggested rascal had given false evidence

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or rascal
lied means told untruths, as a dishonest witness does

explanation.surface: A rogue's testimony in court turned out to be untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Implied means hinted at or indicated indirectly, a synonym of suggested.

clue.text: Died? We are going to live

parts.note: we'll is short for we will, meaning we are going to

explanation.surface: Asked whether someone died, they reply that they intend to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of WE'LL is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or live somewhere.

clue.text: Girl with sex appeal is to move clumsily

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
umph is a variant spelling of oomph, meaning sex appeal

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman has to walk awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: To galumph, a Lewis Carroll coinage, is to stomp along heavily and awkwardly.

clue.text: Lead up the garden path and overturn shed full of fibres

indicators.note: overturn means the built string is flipped and read backwards
full of says the fibres fill the inside of the word for shed

parts.note: to emit is to give off or shed
tow is coarse flax or hemp fibre

explanation.surface: Someone is deceived and told to topple a garden shed stuffed with fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' fills the verb with the fibre to give EMITOWT, which 'overturn' reverses; 'shed' is a verb, not a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone up the garden path is to deceive them, as a cheating partner does.

clue.text: Gold tends to be seen in the city

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
leans means inclines or tends towards

explanation.surface: Gold is a feature of urban life, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a French city on the Loire, famous for Joan of Arc.

clue.text: Mentor deeply disturbed by transfer

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher is deeply upset at being moved to another post.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeployment is moving staff or troops to a new role or place, a kind of transfer.
